# /run-pipeline — eBay Car Part Pipeline

Sequential chain delegation: Agent 1 → Agent 2 → Agent 3.

**Do not edit this file, and do not edit any configuration.** You are the coordinator: you delegate
and you write the three output files in `./output/`. Nothing else. On previous runs a coordinator
overwrote this file with a three-line stub and destroyed every guardrail below, and another edited
`.pi/settings.json` trying to fix a model error mid-run. Both made things worse.

Specifically, never touch: this file, `.pi/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, anything in
`.pi/agents/`, or `.pi/extensions/`. If a run fails, **stop and report the error verbatim** — do not
diagnose it, do not edit config to work around it, do not retry with altered settings. Configuration
here is deliberate and was arrived at painfully; a plausible-looking fix will undo work you cannot
see.

## Launching pi for this job

```
cd "/Users/tamaugo/Desktop/ebay-pipeline/harness"
pi
```

No flags. **Do NOT pass `-ne`** — it disables extension discovery and would strip the `subagent`
tool this orchestration depends on. Older notes say to launch with `-ne -e ...`; that advice is
obsolete as of 2026-09-04 and now actively wrong.

The tool-name collision it worked around (the global `pi-interactive-subagents` and the project-local
`@baryonlabs/pi-agent-harness` both register `subagent`) is now fixed properly in `.pi/settings.json`,
which force-unloads the global package's extension for this project only. If that entry is ever lost,
nothing here will run. `.pi/settings.json` also caps `meta/muse-spark-1.3` at 16,384 max output
tokens — without that cap OpenRouter rejects every Agent 2 and Agent 3 call with a 402, because pi
otherwise requests the model's advertised 943,718-token ceiling, which exceeds the API key's budget.

**Do NOT pass `--tools`** on a pipeline run — it is a strict allowlist and would disable the built-in
read/write tools this orchestration needs. `EBAY_APP_ID` and `EBAY_CERT_ID` must be set in the shell
*before* launching pi; child agents inherit pi's environment.

## Delegation settings — use these on EVERY subagent call

```
agentScope: "both"
confirmProjectAgents: false
```

`agentScope` defaults to `"user"`, but all three agents are project-local, so omitting it makes the
call fail and wastes turns rediscovering why. `confirmProjectAgents` defaults to `true`, which stops
and asks the operator before every agent — unnecessary here.

## Keep coordination cheap

On a previous run the coordinator cost $0.059 while the agent it was coordinating cost $0.0043 —
fourteen times the price of the actual work, almost all of it avoidable exploration.

- **Do not rediscover configuration.** Everything about the setup is stated here. Do not `ls` the
  agents directory, do not `grep` agent frontmatter, do not inspect `.pi/`.
- **But DO look at the input data.** Listing the photo folder and the output folder is required
  work, not exploration. The rule above is about configuration you have already been told; it never
  applies to the images you are being asked to process. A previous run read it too broadly, never
  listed `photos/`, guessed at a filename pattern, matched nothing, and reported an empty folder
  that held four images. **Never conclude a folder is empty without listing it.**
- The three agents are `agent1-part-reader`, `agent2-ebay-lookup`, `agent3-compiler`. They exist,
  they are project-local, they are configured correctly. Take that as given.
- `./photos` holds the images. `./output` is the output folder.
- Delegate, write the file, move on. Do not re-read a file you just wrote, do not summarise
  intermediate results to yourself, and do not verify an agent's work beyond the counts asked for.

## Finding the photos — read this before listing anything

Image files in this project are usually **uppercase `.JPEG`**, and filenames **may contain spaces**.
Both have caused a run to fail by reporting an empty folder that was not empty.

- **Never glob for lowercase extensions.** `photos/*.jpg` and `photos/*.jpeg` match nothing here even
  though the files exist, because globbing is case-sensitive regardless of the filesystem.
- **List the directory itself** (`ls photos/`) rather than globbing by extension, and ignore
  `.DS_Store`.
- **Always quote paths.** `"photos/0118 part number.JPEG"`, never `photos/0118 part number.JPEG`.
- If a folder looks empty, **say what command you ran and stop** — do not conclude it is empty. It
  has been wrong every time so far.

## Inputs (ask the user if not already given)

- Car make and year (required — Agent 1 needs it for its format sanity check)
- Photo folder (default `./photos`), output folder (default `./output`)

Pipeline rule: one folder = one make/year. Confirm both before running against unfamiliar data.

## Steps

1. Delegate to `agent1-part-reader` with every image in the photo folder plus the stated car make.
2. Write its response verbatim to `<output>/agent1_results.md`. Do not edit, reformat or reorder it.
3. Confirm every image has a line. Agent 1's own rules say N images in → N result blocks out, so a
   mismatch is a real bug — surface it, never silently fix it.
4. Delegate to `agent2-ebay-lookup`, passing the full contents of `agent1_results.md`.
5. Write Agent 2's response verbatim to `<output>/agent2_results.md`.
6. Check the line count against step 3. **One filename may legitimately appear on several lines** —
   complementary left/right parts come back separately. That is expected, not a duplicate.
7. Delegate to `agent3-compiler`, passing the contents of `agent2_results.md` **and the output path**
   `<output>/agent3_results.md`. Agent 3 writes that file itself.
8. Confirm `agent3_results.md` exists and its line count equals step 6's.
9. Report briefly: images in; Agent 1 failures; Agent 2 failures **split by type** (`No eBay Listing
   Found` vs `eBay Lookup Unavailable` — these mean different things and must be counted separately);
   Agent 3 malformed-line failures; final line count.

## Notes

- **Agent 2 is live-validated** (2026-09-03): it calls `ebay_search` itself and returns real UK
  listing data with its own tie-break applied. Active listings only — no sold-price source connected.
- **`getRateLimits` is a stub.** It always reports quota fine. Safe at test volume only.
- **Agent 3 is validated against fixtures** (15/15) but not yet against a live pipeline run.
- **Cost scales quadratically with batch size** — each agent processes a whole batch in one
  conversation. An 80-part job costs ~3.2x a 40-part job, not 2x. Chunking at ~10 parts per run
  collapses this; deferred post-demo. See `docs/Agent 2 Model & Cost Decision Record.docx`.
- To A/B an agent's model, edit the single `model:` line in its `.pi/agents/*.md`. Avoid
  `meta/muse-spark-1.2` with a thinking suffix — its reasoning endpoint is blocked by account policy.
